text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- New Singapore $500 million Senior Care Fund set up to aid elderly with medical problems.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton calls for deeper links with China an reaffirms Washington's commitment to Asia-Pacific region.
- Singapore students top maths and science in 45-country survey of 13 year-olds.
- Singapore's non-oil domestic exports in October record 1.1 percent year-on-year growth.
- Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd says plans to acquire a 19.1 percent stake in Malaysian stockbroking firm Rashid Hussain Bhd for Malaysian $15.80 per share.
- Listed Fist Capital Corp offers top Singapore $87.3 million bid in state tender for Robinson Road site.
- Homegrown multimedia rivals Creative Technology and Aztech Systems have both won enthusiastic response to new products at Comdex Fall '96 computer show.
- Singapore Tourist Promotion Board cuts visitor growth forecast for this year to 2 percent.
- Trade in Aztech shares triples amid uncertainty over the fate of the troubled multimedia company.
- Resistor maker ASJ Holdings plans to increase plant capacity by some 50 percent next year and build up distribution network in Malaysia and Thailand to boost direct sales.
- Distributor and manufacturer Ossia International closes at 12 percent above offer price of Singapore 61 cents.
- Transport-based Comfort Group posts a 23.2 percent rise in net operating profit to Singapore $16 million for interim ending September 30.
